aboutCompetition: Hult Prize is a global competition for student entrepreneurs. Teams of two to four build a for-profit business that addresses a UN Sustainable Development Goal, then pitch it in four minutes.
The journey starts with the campus round. Up to three teams can represent UWindsor at Nationals, with a path to the global final and $1 million USD in seed funding.
Teams are judged on both their business and its impact. The aim is to solve a social or environmental problem with a business that can sustain itself.
aboutWindsor: The program runs from October 1, 2026, to April 11, 2027. Five workshop sessions run from November 7 through January 9, with a touch base on January 2. We offer mentor and team matching, host the Grand Finale on February 5, and prepare teams for Nationals in Calgary on April 10–11. The Uwill Discover Conference is on March 13.

Entry, workshops and mentoring are free. The top three teams receive $1,000, $500 and $250. Up to three teams can represent UWindsor at Nationals. The winning team’s travel is covered. Prize money and travel are sponsored separately, so program funding goes directly toward running the competition.
yearOne: UWindsor joined Hult Prize in 2025–2026, led by founding Campus Director Godswisdom Ogbonna. Fourteen student startups registered, and six pitched at the Grand Finale to judges from Windsor’s business community.

Mycovolt and 100% Fish advanced to the Canadian National Championships at McGill University in Montreal. 100% Fish finished in Canada’s top eight. The Hult Prize Foundation named UWindsor the Best Program in North America.
Ten partners contributed $8,000 to run the first season.
yearPlan: Our second season focuses on supporting more student teams, from their first workshop to the Grand Finale and Nationals.
Our targets: 20 registered startups, at least 10 finalists and a minimum of $10,000 in program funding. We’ll report the results at the end of the season.
yearBenefits: Free workshops, mentoring and help finding a team.

Five workshop sessions run from November 7 to January 9, covering problem definition, business models, pitch decks and delivery. Teams have a touch base on January 2 and pitch to Windsor business leaders at the Grand Finale on February 5. The Uwill Discover Conference follows on March 13.
Up to three teams can represent UWindsor at Nationals in Calgary on April 10–11, with nine weeks to prepare after the Grand Finale. The program runs through April 11, 2027.
competeIntro: Start with an idea and a team of 2–4 students. Free workshops run from November 7 to January 9. Up to three teams can represent UWindsor at Nationals on April 10–11. No company, prototype or business degree required.
Only one teammate needs to study at UWindsor. Students from other universities can join your team.
eligibility: Teams of two to four people.
Every member must be a student, undergraduate or graduate.
Everyone must be 18 or older by February 28, 2027.
At least one member must be enrolled at the University of Windsor. The others do not have to be.
Your venture must be for-profit and address at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal.
steps: 1. Sign up below. Get updates on deadlines, workshops and team matching.
2. Register officially at hultprize.org/register. Complete this step to enter the competition.
3. Build your team. You need two to four students. If you’re looking for teammates, join the team matching chat below.
4. Join the group chat. Get reminders and updates for registered teams.
5. Attend the workshops. Sessions are free. Choose the ones your team needs.
noTeam: Tell us your program, year and skills, and whether you have an idea or want to join a team. We’ll introduce you to potential teammates.
faq: Does it cost anything?  No. Entry, workshops and mentoring are free.
Is there a cash prize at the campus round?  Yes. The top three teams take home $1,000, $500 and $250. The winning team’s travel to Nationals is also covered.
How many teams can go to Nationals?  Up to three teams can represent UWindsor at Nationals in Calgary on April 10–11.
Do I need to be in business school?  No. Students from any program can enter.
What if my idea changes?  That’s part of the process. Use the workshops and mentor feedback to test and improve it.
How much time does this take?  Workshops run about an hour and you choose which to attend. The pitch itself is four minutes.
Can someone from another university be on my team?  Yes. Every teammate must be a student and 18 or older by February 28, 2027. At least one teammate must be enrolled at UWindsor.
partnersYear: Ten organisations funded our first season. Fourteen startups entered, six reached the Grand Finale and two advanced to Nationals. 100% Fish placed in Canada’s top eight, and UWindsor was named the Best Program in North America.
This season, we’re targeting 20 startups, at least 10 finalists on February 5 and $10,000 in program funding. Cash prizes and the winning team’s travel are sponsored separately.
partnersBenefits: Partners receive an opt-in participant directory after the Grand Finale, with permission to contact students about opportunities.
Judging packages include a seat on February 5. Hear the pitches, question the teams and help select up to three teams to represent UWindsor at Nationals. Allow three to four hours.
Every partner receives an impact report within a month of the Grand Finale, covering participating ventures, campus results, photos and how funds were spent.
partnersVentures: Mycovolt and 100% Fish both reached Nationals in our first season. Both ventures continue to operate in Windsor.
funding: Program funding covers venues, workshops, mentoring, materials and the Grand Finale. Cash prizes and the winning team’s travel to Calgary are sponsored separately.

Nationals Travel Partner, by agreement.  Covers the winning team's travel to the National Championships in Calgary on April 10–11, 2027. Named when the winner is announced and in everything the team does at Nationals.

Supporter, $500.  Logo on the website and the Finals program, and thanks across our channels.

tierReport: Impact report within a month of the Grand Finale.

otherSupport: Judge the Grand Finale on February 5, mentor a team for two or three hours between December and late January, or lead a workshop. We also welcome space, services and introductions to local supporters.
